'''Joseph Clois Shivers Jr.''' (November 29, 1920 – September 1, 2014) was an American textile chemist who was based in [[West Chester, Pennsylvania]], best known for his role in the structural development of [[Spandex]], a thermoplastic elastomer, in the 1950s, while employed at [[DuPont]].<ref name="olneybio" />

Shivers was born in 1920 in [[Marlton, New Jersey]]. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]], [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] and [[Ph.D.]] (in organic chemistry) from [[Duke University]] in the 1940s.<ref name="olneybio">{{cite journal |author=American Association of Textile Chemists and Colorists |date=August 1998 |title=Joseph C. Shivers To Receive the Olney Medal |journal=Textile Chemist and Colorist |volume=30 |issue=8 |page=57 |url=http://www.aatcc.org/awards/OlneyShivers.pdf |access-date=July 30, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203014041/http://www.aatcc.org/awards/OlneyShivers.pdf |archive-date=December 3, 2013 }}</ref> During the course of the war, still as a student, he worked with the United States government to develop a drug to counter [[malaria]] for use by troops overseas.<ref name="philly">{{cite web|url=http://articles.philly.com/1991-04-15/business/25780636_1_lycra-fiber-graduate-student |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204074329/http://articles.philly.com/1991-04-15/business/25780636_1_lycra-fiber-graduate-student |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 4, 2013 |title=His Discovery Gave The World New Shapes|publisher=Articles.philly.com |date=1991-04-15 |access-date=2013-07-30}}</ref> Shivers began working for [[DuPont]] in 1946 as a researcher on polymers. After working on other polyester projects, Shivers joined a project to synthesize a "synthetic elastomer to replace rubber", which was common in garments at the time.<ref name="olneybio" /> Though the project was shelved at some point, Shivers made a breakthrough in the 1950s when he attempted a modification of the polyester [[Dacron]], which produced a stretchy fibre that could withstand heat, be spun into filaments, and stretch 5 times its original length while retaining elasticity.<ref name="philly" /> The results were favorable and Shivers, along with other employees, set out to perfect the new polyester.<ref name="olneybio" /> In 1959 it was completed and released under the name Fibre K, later changed to [[Lycra]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0qFQ5OuKoy8C&pg=PA149 |title=Polymer Chemistry: Introduction to an Indispensable Science|author=David M. Teegarden  |publisher=NSTA Press|year= 2004|page=149|isbn=9780873552219}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nmHzgroEYIwC&pg=PA287 |title=Introduction to Polymer Chemistry |author=Charles E. Carraher, Jr.|publisher=CRC Press|year=2013|page=287|isbn=9781466554948 }}</ref> He was promoted to supervisor after the breakthrough.<ref name="philly" /> It was commercialized by DuPont in 1962 and became widespread in the garment industry, including sports garments, swimsuits, hosiery and undergarments.<ref name="olneybio" /> By the early 1990s, Lycra was one of the most lucrative facets of the synthetic fiber department at Dupont.<ref name="philly" /> Shivers was also on the faculty of [[Canisius College]] while working at DuPont. He retired from DuPont in 1980, as technical director of the fiber department.<ref name="olneybio" />

In 1998, he was awarded the prestigious Olney Medal for Achievement in Textile Chemistry for his work by the [[American Association of Textile Chemists and Colorists]], the 55th recipient of the medal in its history.<ref name="olneybio" /> Shivers was presented with it in a ceremony in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]] at an AATCC Conference. His Olney Medal Address was entitled "The Search for a Superior Elastic Fibre".<ref name="olneybio" /><ref>Harold A. Wittcoff, ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=ee6qcTC8o_sC&pg=PA184&dq=joseph+shivers+dupont&sig=0F2PBLHVNS_l-V-f3z4yVUyhf4k Organic Chemistry Principles and Industrial Practice],'' 184.</ref> [[DuPont]] awarded Shivers with their Lavoisier Medal in 1995, the highest honor for the company.<ref name="olneybio" />

He was married to Margaret Warren Shivers, originally from Ohio; with her he had three children. In his leisure time, he enjoyed woodworking and [[wine tasting]].<ref name="olneybio" /> He was a member of the fraternity [[Phi Beta Kappa]] as well as the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name="olneybio" /> On September 1, 2014, Shivers died in [[Venice, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/heraldtribune/obituary.aspx?n=joseph-clois-shivers&pid=172355529&fhid=9074 |title=Joseph Clois Shivers Jr. |work=Obituary, Herald Tribune |date=4 September 2014 |publisher=Legacy.com}}</ref>
